notes: Sourced primarily from Daktronics' own All Sport 5000 Series Operation Manual (ED-11976, Rev 32, 04 Nov 2024), specifically Appendix A drawing DWG-102142 "Rear View, A/S 5010 Connector Assignments" (title block: "ALL SPORT 5000 SERIES CONSOLES"), which Daktronics documents as the rear-panel/connector reference for the whole All Sport 5000 series (models 5010=120VAC, 5020=230VAC, 5012=12VDC). Physical dimensions (4.25"H x 16.25"W x 9"D), weight (7 lb), and power (120/240 VAC, 6 W) cross-checked against the shorter Daktronics product spec sheet SL-03991. This is a desktop scoring/timing control console, not rack-mountable (rackUnits omitted). No graded connector types apply (no HDMI/SDI/USB/Ethernet/DisplayPort ports present), so no "grade" field was set on any port, per instructions. Two front-panel cutouts seen on the rear-view drawing, J5 "Computer I/O Port" and J8 "Switch Inputs", are explicitly labeled "NOT USED ON THIS MODEL" and were omitted as non-functional. Several connector-taxonomy approximations were needed since the console predates modern AV standards and uses Daktronics-proprietary 20 mA current-loop scoreboard signaling: the J1-J3 "Scoreboard Outputs" are 1/4" phone jacks (trs-6.35) but carry current-loop signal, not audio; J4/J7 remote start/stop switch jacks are actually 6-pin modular (RJ12-style) jacks, approximated to rj45 (closest/only modular-jack option in the taxonomy); and J6 "Main Output and Input Port" is physically a 25-pin D-sub (DB25) combining RS-232 with current-loop and relay/switch signals, approximated to rs232 as the closest single listed connector (full DB25 pinout given in the port note). These approximations are noted individually on each affected port.

ports.name: Scoreboard Output 1 (J1)
ports.note: 1/4" phone jack wired Tip=Current Loop Output+, Ring=Current Loop Output-, Sleeve=GND — a proprietary 20 mA current-loop scoreboard drive signal, not analog audio.

ports.name: Scoreboard Output 2 (J2)
ports.note: Same wiring/function as J1 (current-loop scoreboard drive, not audio).

ports.name: Scoreboard Output 3 (J3)
ports.note: Same wiring/function as J1 (current-loop scoreboard drive, not audio).

ports.name: Main Clock Start/Stop/Horn Switch (J4)
ports.note: Physically a 6-pin modular (RJ12/RJ25-style, 6P6C) control jack for the optional remote clock switch accessory — not Ethernet/8P8C. rj45 chosen as closest listed connector (no RJ11/12 option in taxonomy).

ports.name: Main Output and Input Port (J6)
ports.note: Physically a 25-pin D-sub (DB25), not DB9. Combo port: pins 2/3/7 carry RS-232 serial TX/RX/GND; remaining pins carry 4 channels of 20 mA current-loop scoreboard output, 1 current-loop input, a relay output, a switch input, and a 10V AC/DC power-sense input. rs232 chosen as closest single listed connector type — no generic multi-signal D-sub/current-loop option exists in the taxonomy.

ports.name: Shot Clock Start/Stop/Reset Switch (J7)
ports.note: Same 6-pin modular (RJ12-style) jack type as J4, for the optional remote shot-clock switch accessory.

ports.name: AC Power In
ports.note: Captive 8 ft (2.44 m) three-prong power cord (not a detachable IEC inlet) on the standard 120 VAC (All Sport 5010) variant. The 240 VAC export variant (All Sport 5020) uses a different captive-cord/inlet arrangement — confirm for your specific regional unit.
